title: Dilucidationes super methodo elegantissima, qua illustris de la Grange usus est in integranda aequatione differentiali dx/√X = dy/√Y

deep.reconstruction:
Page 12 of E506 continues 'Alia solutio facillima', a short solution of the separated Riccati-type equation dx/(a+2bx+cxx) + dy/(a+2by+cyy) = 0 using Lagrange's auxiliary variable t.

Set X = a+2bx+cx², Y = a+2by+cy², and let dx/dt = X, dy/dt = −Y, which is equivalent to the given equation. Put p = x+y, q = x−y, u = xy.

§24. dp/dt = X − Y = 2b(x−y) + c(x²−y²) = q(2b+cp), so dp/(2b+cp) = q dt.

§25. du/dt = yX − xY = a(y−x) + cxy(x−y) = q(cu−a), so du/(cu−a) = q dt. Eliminating q dt gives dp/(2b+cp) = du/(cu−a). This integrates to log(2b+cp) = log(cu−a) + log C, i.e. the bilinear (bidegree (1,1)) algebraic integral (2b+c(x+y))/(cxy−a) = C. Euler calls this the 'simplest form'. It is reached directly, without the second differentials of the earlier §§ (Lagrange's original route) and without the factor reduction of §23. He remarks that the 'first case' cannot be solved this way.

§26. Adding 2b/a gives a constant multiple of (a(x+y)+2bxy)/(cxy−a). Dividing one form by the other gives (2b+c(x+y))/(a(x+y)+2bxy) = C. Euler verifies the last form by differentiation. The numerator of the differential is −2ab(dx+dy) − 4b²(y dx + x dy) − 2bc(y²dx + x²dy). Setting it to zero and dividing by 2b gives Y dx + X dy = 0, i.e. the proposed equation.

In modern terms, the general integral is the one-parameter family of Möbius (projective) correspondences y = (αx+β)/(γx+δ) preserving the quadratic form. It is the 'addition theorem' of the degenerate (genus-0) case, the rational analogue of Euler's elliptic addition theorem.
errors: No mathematical errors found; every step checks.
Minor: integrating dp/(2b+cp) = du/(cu−a) each side carries a factor 1/c, which Euler silently drops because it cancels.

The closing remark that 'the first case' cannot be treated this way is not explained on this page. Its referent (presumably the original quartic-radical / elliptic case, or some special case treated earlier) cannot be fixed from this page alone.

ideas.what: Introducing an auxiliary 'time' t so that a separated equation becomes a pair of ODEs dx/dt = X, dy/dt = ±Y, then forming symmetric functions p = x+y, u = xy (and q = x−y)
ideas.modern_name: Lagrange's method for algebraic integrals of Euler's equation (symmetric-function / auxiliary-parameter method)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lagrange (Miscellanea Taurinensia, c. 1766–69); Euler's elaboration in E506
ideas.where_published: E506 itself (Acta Acad. Sci. Petrop. 1780); related treatment in E505/E506 era papers

ideas.what: First-order shortcut: dp/(2b+cp) = q dt = du/(cu−a) gives the integral without second differentials
ideas.modern_name: Elimination of the common factor q dt to obtain a first integral directly (an integrating ratio)

ideas.what: Bilinear algebraic integral (2b+c(x+y))/(cxy−a) = C, with equivalent forms obtained by adding a constant and taking quotients, and checked by differentiation
ideas.modern_name: Addition law of the genus-0 (Möbius / projective) case; one-parameter group of fractional linear transformations
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (rational case of the addition theorem, 1750s–60s, e.g. Institutiones calculi integralis)
ideas.where_published: Institutiones calculi integralis vol. I (E342) and Euler's papers on the integration of dx/√X = dy/√Y

deep.surprise_reason: A clean, correct but elementary first-order shortcut within a published, well-known paper; the rational case of Euler's addition theorem is standard and nothing here is unrecorded.
